newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Wool seen accelerating technology take-up - IWS.
newsitem.headline: Wool seen accelerating technology take-up - IWS.

text.p: Wool's fightback against loss of market share to cotton and synthetic materials is involving accelerated take-up of new technologies by growers and industry, John Grant, technical director of the International Wool Secretariat (IWS), told the annual wool forum here on Monday.
Main competitors cotton and chemical fibres were achieving annual productivity gains three times greater than wool, he said.
In the first year of its new technical strategy, the IWS was overhauling its A$30 million research and development programme to accelerate the adoption of new technologies, he said.
"Improving the productivity of growers and downstream users of wool is critical to the future of this industry," Grant said.
IWS had identified about A$250 million in savings that could flow to growers if they and others along the pipeline adopted innovations in wool production and processing, he said.
The IWS technical strategy, adopted in 1996, is designed to increase the speed and rate at which industry adopts new technologies, as well as to generate new ideas.
IWS had reduced the number of research and development projects for 1997 to 100 from 330 in 1996 and expected to have only 50 in 1998, he said.
IWS established a technical adoption team during 1996 to attack poor rates of on-farm technical adoption and was also setting up centres of technical excellence in Europe and Asia.

The first will be established at Ichinomiya in Japan from the middle of this year and will involve IWS technical representatives working on-site with industyry representatives. A European centre at Biella, Italy, is expected to be operational later this year, he said.
